alternatives.name: Functional syntax as the primary form
alternatives.description: Use Point2D = TypedDict('Point2D', x=int, y=int) as the only way to define TypedDicts, without the class-based syntax.
alternatives.reason_rejected: The functional form is harder for static type checkers to analyze and doesn't support inheritance or method definitions.

alternatives.name: Use NamedTuple instead of TypedDict
alternatives.description: Use NamedTuple for all cases where structured data with typed fields is needed.
alternatives.reason_rejected: NamedTuples are immutable and create new objects. TypedDict describes plain dicts which are mutable and already widely used in Python codebases, especially for JSON data.

alternatives.name: Use regular classes with __init__ annotations
alternatives.description: Define typed dictionary-like objects as regular classes with annotated __init__ parameters.
alternatives.reason_rejected: This doesn't match the actual runtime type (dict). TypedDict specifically describes the structure of plain dict objects.

objections.text: TypedDict adds another way to define structured types alongside dataclasses, NamedTuple, and regular classes, increasing cognitive load.
